The owning system owns each file **by review (CODEOWNERS-style entry in `tools/lint/config/owners.json`), not by import.** | no |
124	| `src/kernel/` | L1 | Kernel, `TickDriver`, `ProcessPriority`, registries, `SimViews`, `WriteScope`, contexts, descriptors, `Command` (ADR-0001 to 0004). Subdirectories: `facets/` (classes the composition root hands to other layers: `PresentationClock`, `SurfaceHandle`, `ControlHandle`, `ModuleFacet`, `BlockRegistrar`, `ChangeBatch`), `ports/` (abstract interfaces the kernel needs injected, e.g. `Clock`), `testing/` (§ 4.3). | no |
125	| `src/data/` | L1 | `ContentLoader`, `ContentSource` and its two implementations, schemas, catalogs, `ContentFaults`, per-domain subfolders such as `src/data/items/` (ADR-0007). | no |
126	| `src/save/` | L1 | Save/Load host service. May use `FileAccess`, `DirAccess`, `Thread`, `JSON`, `HashingContext` (allow-list `IO-01`). | no |
127	| `src/sim/<system>/` | L2 | One directory per simulation module: `graph`, `layout`, `body`, `emitter`, `controller`, `interaction`, `suit`, `assembly`, `web`, `attention`, `horror`, `sanity` (IC-10: `src/sim/sanity/`, never `src/sanity/`). Each may hold `views/` (read-view facades and value types that presentation may name), `ports/` (abstract interfaces other modules may name), `testing/` (test seams) and internals (blocks, mutators, hooks, `*_faults.gd`). | no |
128	| `src/presentation/<system>/` | L3 | `pipeline`, `perception`, `lighting`, `trail`, `hud`, `instruments`, `chart`, `audio`, `controller` (Input Adapter and Avatar Presenter), `projector` (Layout PROJECTOR and `body.projector`). | yes |
129	| `src/game/` | L4 | The composition root `game.gd` (ADR-0001), `KernelHost` (`src/game/kernel_host.gd`; the only `Node` that drives the tick), `MonotonicClock` (the production `Clock`), the dev-build boot walks (§ 6.5), the guarded dev loaders. The one place allowed to name every layer. | yes |
130	| `src/debug/`, `src/observer/` | dev | Debug Overlay and observer log (ADR-0031). Reached only by the guarded runtime `load()` in `src/game/` after `ResourceLoader.exists()` (TR-debug-037); their root script declares no `class_name`. | yes |
131	
132	**1.2 Placement decisions that were open.**
133	- **The PROJECTOR scripts live in `src/presentation/projector/`**, not in `src/sim/layout/` or `src/sim/body/`. This makes `src/sim/**` a tree-free directory with no per-file exception, so BDY-3's "the PROJECTOR script is the only Body script allowed to name `Node2D`, `Camera2D` or `Viewport`" becomes "no script under `src/sim/body/` names them". ADR-0034 still owns the scene shape.
134	- **`KernelHost` lives in `src/game/`**, so `src/kernel/` carries no `Node` and the kernel GDD's lint ("no block or kernel source references `Node`, `SceneTree`, `get_tree` or `Engine.get_main_loop`") has no exception. If ADR-0001 places it in `src/kernel/`, `SIM-01` allow-lists exactly that one file.
135	- **Shared pure helpers live in `src/shared/`**, importable by `src/data/` and every layer, because `src/data/` may not import `src/sim/` and loaders need the Graph's `connectable`. `IntMath` is the one place that divides integers (§ 5.4).
136	- **Scenes (`.tscn`) are allowed only** under `src/presentation/`, `src/game/`, `src/debug/`, `src/observer/`; scripts attached to a scene must be in the same set. No `.tscn` sets `process_priority` (ADR-0001).
137	- **Tests are not under `src/`** (`src/CLAUDE.md`): `tests/unit/<system>/`, `tests/integration/<system>/`, `tests/render/`, `tests/fixtures/`, `tests/support/`. Fakes and doubles (`FakeClock`, `FakeCollide`, `WorkCounter` doubles, stubs) live in `tests/support/`, never in `src/`.
138	- **Typing conventions the warnings force** (`UNUSED_PARAMETER`, `UNTYPED_DECLARATION` at 2): an unused parameter is `_`-prefixed (this includes parameters of port implementations and doubles); `for` iterators are typed (`for i: int in n`; an untyped iterator is a load error, P3). The snippets in § Key Interfaces follow this.
139	- **Naming.** One `class_name` per file; the file name is the snake_case of the class name; `*_faults.gd` for fault domains (ADR-0003); abstract ports are named for the role (`Clock`, `SolidQuery`, `OccluderSource`), not `IClock`. A script referenced by another script has a `class_name`.
140	
141	**1.3 Tools.** Headless GDScript tools live under `tools/`: `tools/lint/` (this ADR), `tools/ci/` (ADR-0007's `content_lint.gd`, the item-database and Derelict content rule packs, `load_all.gd`, `lane_report.gd`), `tools/asset-pipeline/` (generators, ADR-0007 § 2.6). A tool enumerating `src/`, `tests/` or `tools/` is **not** the forbidden `content_directory_scan`, which bans *game code* enumerating `res://assets/data`.

143	### 2. Dependency direction and import edges
144	
145	**2.1 What an edge is.** The lint tool builds a module-level graph from `ProjectSettings.get_global_class_list()` (class name to defining file) and, per file, every `class_name` token that survives comment and string stripping, plus every `preload(`/`load(`/`ResourceLoader` target. A file in module A that names a class defined in module B is an A to B edge. (Tier E2 with an E3 class map; a class named only inside a comment or string is not an edge; a class reached only through a `Variant` is not seen, which the engine tier covers because `UNSAFE_*` is an error.)
146	
147	**2.2 The matrix.** "Y" means allowed; blank means a finding (`ARCH-02`).
148	
149	| from \ to | shared | kernel (core) | kernel/facets, kernel/ports | data | save | sim/X views, ports | sim/X internals | presentation | game | debug, observer |
150	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
151	| shared | Y | | | | | | | | | |
152	| kernel | Y | Y | Y | | | | | | | |
153	| data | Y | | | Y | | | | | | |
154	| save | Y | Y | Y | | Y | Y (views, ports only) | | | | |
155	| sim/X | Y | Y | Y | Y | | Y | own module and other sim modules | | | |
156	| presentation/X | Y | | Y | Y | | Y | | Y | | |
157	| game | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | guarded load only |
158	| debug, observer | Y | | Y | Y | | Y | | Y | | Y |
159	| tests | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y (integration tests boot the composition root) | |
160	
161	Reading the rules the architecture states in prose:
162	1. **Simulation to simulation, any direction, module granularity** (architecture rule 1). The matrix does not police which sim module calls which; the kernel's step-hook topo-sort polices acyclicity of hooks. A call into another module is by `class_name`, never `preload`.
163	2. **No compile-time cycles of `preload`** (architecture rule 2): `ARCH-03` bans `preload`, `load` and `ResourceLoader` of any `.gd` path anywhere in `src/` (use `class_name`). Probe P9 shows `class_name` cycles load, so cycles are not the risk this rule polices; hidden coupling is, and the matrix polices that.
164	3. **Foundation host services read Feature state only through the kernel** (rule 3): `save` has no edge to `sim/X` internals and never imports a module. Save/Load obtains owner read views through the kernel registry, and may *type* those variables with the published `sim/<x>/views/**` and `sim/<x>/ports/**` classes; naming a published view class is not importing the module. Every other `save` to `sim` reference is an `ARCH-02` finding (assumption for ADR-0006).
165	4. **Simulation never reads presentation** (rule 4): no sim edge to `presentation`, `game`, `debug`, `observer`. Presentation reaches the simulation only through `sim/<x>/views/**` and `sim/<x>/ports/**` classes, and reaches the kernel only through `kernel/facets/**`. It never names `Kernel`, `SimViews`, `WriteScope`, `Command`, any `*Context`, `BlockDescriptor` (ADR-0003 risk "a facet leak"; `ARCH-08`).
166	5. **`data` imports `shared` only** (ADR-0007 constraint): no `sim`, no `kernel`. The kernel tick rate reaches the loader as a constructor argument.
167	6. **Nothing imports `game`, `debug` or `observer`** except through the guarded load in `game/`.
168	7. **`Kernel`, `KernelHost`, `TickDriver` are named only in `kernel/` and `game/`** (registry `kernel_autoload_or_global`; `ARCH-08`). **`Command.new(` appears only in `src/kernel/`** (registry `command_constructed_outside_kernel`; `KRN-02`).
169	
170	**2.3 Module and directory list is data.** The set of module directories, the matrix and the facet/port/view sub-directory names are committed in `tools/lint/config/modules.json` and `tools/lint/config/edges.json`; adding a module is a reviewed edit to those files in the same change as the first file (`ARCH-01`).
171	
172	### 3. Interface mechanism: `@abstract` ports
173	
174	**3.1 The choice.** A seam that is injected and that tests must double is an **`@abstract` base class, a "port"**, living in the `ports/` directory of the lowest layer that every consumer of the contract may import (the lowest layer that every consumer may import: `src/kernel/ports/` for `Clock`, which `src/sim`, `src/presentation` and `src/game` all reach; `src/sim/layout/ports/` for `OccluderSource`). Implementations `extends` the port; test doubles `extends` the port. A port is `RefCounted`, holds only `@abstract` methods, constants and (rarely) a documented non-abstract default; it holds no fields. The consumer types its `setup()` parameter as the port.
175	
176	Probed on 4.7.2 (P4): a subclass that omits an abstract method fails at parse time, which is the strongest guarantee available without a custom tool; direct construction of the port fails at parse time. The reflective `GDScript.new()` bypass is accepted: no game code constructs through reflection.
177	
178	**3.2 What it does not replace.**
179	- **ADR-0003 §1 stands.** Kernel-invoked owner callables (`validate`, `apply`, `hook`, `snapshot`, `restore`, ...) remain registered `Callable`s ending `return ctx.complete()`. That choice rested on many callables per owner, no inheritance coupling and stubs that register plain callables, not only on `@abstract` being unexercised. There is no `BlockOwner` port.
180	- **Ports are for injected collaborators**, not for owner callables and not for block contents: `Clock`, `ContentSource`, `SolidQuery`, `OccluderSource`, `WorkCounter`, `DiagnosticsSink`, `ObserverSink`, and the stub points of TR-pc-045 and TR-charttable-038.
181	- **The duck-typed alternative is kept for one job**: `ContractCheck` (tier E3) compares a double that deliberately does *not* extend a port (a recorded stub for a sibling GDD system) against the real class by reflection (§ 6.4).
182	
183	**3.3 The 4.7 interaction.** An override inherits the base method's typed return and must `return` on every path (breaking-changes, 4.6 to 4.7). For ports this is a feature: a missing `return` in an implementation is a parse error, not a runtime default. Rule: an implementation restates the full signature, including `-> T`; `REFLECT-SIG` (tier E3) compares each implementation's `get_script_method_list()` entry (argument count, defaults, return type id) with the port's, because the engine's own override check is weaker than "identical".
184	
185	**3.4 Fallback.** If LINT-SPIKE-1(a) shows `@abstract` does not survive a release export, ports become plain base classes whose methods call `push_error("ABSTRACT_CALLED")` and return a safe default, and `REFLECT-ABSTRACT` (tier E3, test-time) asserts every port implementation overrides every method named in the port. Call sites do not change. Cost of ports in a hot loop (one extra method dispatch) is measured by S1 (§ 9); ports sit at coarse seams (once per actor per tick, not per tile).
186	
187	### 4. Scene-tree-free simulation and test seams
188	
189	**4.1 What "scene-tree free" means mechanically.** In `src/shared/`, `src/kernel/`, `src/data/`, `src/save/` and `src/sim/**` (all of L0 to L2): no class extends `Node`, `Resource` (blocks and catalogs are `RefCounted`), or any engine node; no token from the tree list (`SIM-01`: `Node`, `Node2D`, `Node3D`, `CanvasItem`, `CanvasLayer`, `Control`, `SceneTree`, `Viewport`, `SubViewport`, `Window`, `Camera2D`, `PackedScene`, `get_tree`, `get_node`, `get_node_or_null`, `find_child`, `add_child`, `queue_free`, `$`, `@onready`, `@export`, `_ready`, `_enter_tree`, `_process`, `_input`, `_unhandled_input`, `Engine.get_main_loop`, `Tween`, `Timer`, `RenderingServer`, `PhysicsServer2D`, `AudioServer`, `DisplayServer`, `Input`, `InputMap`). `SIM-01` carries no waiver. `Thread`, `FileAccess`, `HashingContext` are not in the list; their use is bounded by `IO-01` to `src/save/` and `src/data/`.
190	
191	**4.2 Headless harness.** The simulation is constructed by tests exactly as the composition root does: a `Kernel` with an injected `KernelProfile` (never `OS.is_debug_build()`, TR-cmd-033), an injected `Clock`, injected catalogs from `MemoryContentSource`, and module `setup()` calls with `FakeX` doubles from `tests/support/`. `Kernel.step()` advances synchronously. Two kernels coexist in one process (TR-cmd-052): that is a test, `tests/unit/kernel/lifecycle/`, asserting independent `T`, queues and logs; a block bound to a second kernel fails boot with `BLOCK_ALREADY_BOUND`; `Kernel.dispose()` is idempotent and leaves `OBJECT_COUNT` and the orphan-node count where they started (tier E4, `CNT-01`). `static var` is banned in `src/` (`ARCH-04`) because it is the only way two kernels could share state without the lint noticing it as an edge.
192	
193	**4.3 Test seams in production classes.** `TestIngress.submit_raw`, `debug_set_counters`, the stubbed diagnostics timer, `set_knob`, the `WorkCounter` double hook and the like (TR-cmd-050, TR-emitter-032) live **only** in classes under `src/<module>/testing/` named `Test*`. They are importable only from `tests/` and other `testing/` directories (`ARCH-09`); the release export preset's `exclude_filter` gains `src/*/testing/*` and `src/*/*/testing/*` (the filter list is ADR-0007's `content_export` entry; this ADR adds the two globs). The export check is two-sided: a lexical rule that no non-`testing/` file names a `testing/` class, and an exported-pack file-list scan (mounting the `.pck` and listing `res://src/**`; UNVERIFIED, added to the CONTENT-EXP-1 harness) that finds no `testing/` path.
194	
195	**4.4 No conditional compilation.** GDScript has no preprocessor. "Compiled in solely under the EM_WORK_COUNTER test flag" (TR-emitter-032) is realised by **injection**: a `WorkCounter` port, a counting implementation in `tests/support/`, and `NullWorkCounter` injected in every shipped and benchmarked build. Runtime `OS.has_feature()` tags (ADR-0031) gate dev features; they are not a substitute for exclusion.
196	
197	**4.5 Time and randomness.** Wall-clock, frame counters and global RNG are banned in `src/` (`SIM-02`): `Time.get_ticks_msec`, `Time.get_ticks_usec`, `Time.get_unix_time_from_system`, `Time.get_datetime_dict_from_system`, `Time.get_time_dict_from_system`, `get_process_delta_time`, `Engine.get_frames_drawn`, `Engine.get_process_frames`, `Engine.get_physics_frames`, `randi`, `randf`, `randomize`, `randi_range`, `randf_range`, `RandomNumberGenerator`, `pick_random`, `shuffle`. The allow-list is `src/game/kernel_host.gd` and the diagnostics timer (ADR-0001) **plus `src/game/monotonic_clock.gd`**, the production `Clock` that the Pipeline, Controller and others receive (TR-pxl-031, TR-pc-045). The third entry extends ADR-0001's two-file allow-list and is recorded as a cross-ADR assumption. Time-dependent logic receives `Clock.now_us()` or ticks by injection and tests drive a `FakeClock`.
198	
199	### 5. Static typing and warnings as errors
200	
201	**5.1 The settings.** The engine's analyzer is the authority for type flow (tier E1). `project.godot` pins, under `[debug]`:
202	
203	- **Every `debug/gdscript/warnings/*` severity is 2 (error) except `RETURN_VALUE_DISCARDED`, which is 0.** No warning is left at 1, because a level-1 warning prints nothing headless (P10) and therefore cannot fail CI. The 2s include `UNTYPED_DECLARATION`, `INFERRED_DECLARATION`, `UNSAFE_PROPERTY_ACCESS`, `UNSAFE_METHOD_ACCESS`, `UNSAFE_CAST`, `UNSAFE_CALL_ARGUMENT`, `UNSAFE_VOID_RETURN`, `NARROWING_CONVERSION`, `INTEGER_DIVISION`, `INFERENCE_ON_VARIANT`, `MISSING_AWAIT`, `STATIC_CALLED_ON_INSTANCE`, `UNUSED_VARIABLE`, `UNUSED_PARAMETER`, `UNUSED_PRIVATE_CLASS_VARIABLE`, `UNUSED_SIGNAL`, `SHADOWED_VARIABLE`, `SHADOWED_VARIABLE_BASE_CLASS`, `SHADOWED_GLOBAL_IDENTIFIER`, `UNREACHABLE_CODE`, `STANDALONE_EXPRESSION`, `INT_AS_ENUM_WITHOUT_CAST`, `ENUM_VARIABLE_WITHOUT_DEFAULT`, `NATIVE_METHOD_OVERRIDE`, `REDUNDANT_AWAIT`, `CONFUSABLE_*`, and every other warning the 4.7.2 property list returns (P1). `PRJ-01` compares the live `ProjectSettings` values with `tools/lint/config/warning_levels.json`, so a new warning added by an engine patch release (default 1) fails the check until it is classified.
204	- **`directory_rules = { "res://": 0, "res://addons": 0, "res://tests": 0, "res://src": 1, "res://tools": 1 }`.** `src/` and `tools/` are promoted; `tests/` and `addons/` are excluded. Subdirectories inherit (P3). This settles BDY-3's "[UNV] whether a directory scope exists": it exists on 4.7.2, with include/exclude semantics and global severity.
205	- **One tier of strictness for all of `src/`**, simulation and presentation alike (§ Alternatives 5). Presentation code that needs to name a `Node` type annotates it (`$Label` assigned to a `Label` variable, `get_node("Label") as Label`, a `Dictionary` element assigned to a typed `int`, and `get_child(0)` assigned to `Node` loaded clean in a scratch project with the typing and four `unsafe_*` warnings at 2, probed 2026-10-28; the other warnings were not part of that probe), and uses `IntMath` or `float()` where it divides.
206	- **`PRJ-02` project invariants** (read with `ConfigFile`): `[autoload]` absent or empty; `application/run/low_processor_mode` false (ADR-0001); no `physics_jitter_fix` or `max_physics_steps_per_frame` coupling (ADR-0001, registry `physics_callback_tick_source`); `physics/common/physics_interpolation` false (ADR-0009 forward). Stretch pins are ADR-0008's rule, hosted in the same `PRJ` pack.
207	
208	**5.2 The CI gate is "every script loads".** Promoted warnings fire when a script is parsed (P3). `tools/ci/load_all.gd` enumerates `res://src/**/*.gd` and `res://tools/**/*.gd`, `load()`s each, and fails when the result is null, `can_instantiate()` is false, or the process log contains a `SCRIPT ERROR:` line (a stray promoted warning prints as `Parse Error ... (Warning treated as error.)`). `load()` returns a non-null object even after a parse error (P3), so the `can_instantiate()` check and the log scan are both required; LINT-SPIKE-1(b) confirms `can_instantiate()` for the warning-as-error case. The framework's existing `.claude/scripts/godot-parse-check.gd` is the single-file variant used locally.
209	
210	**5.3 Typing conventions the warnings do not catch** (lexical, `SIM-09`, scoped to `src/shared`, `src/kernel`, `src/sim`): no `Variant`-typed declaration except in allow-listed files (`src/data/*_read.gd`, command payload and snapshot code listed in `tools/lint/config/allowlists/dictionary_variant.json`); no bare `Array`; a bare `Dictionary` only where ADR-0002 (payloads) and ADR-0003 (snapshot, restore) require one; everything else uses `Array[T]` and `Dictionary[K, V]` (4.4; `deprecated-apis.md` "untyped Array/Dictionary"). The sim never iterates a `Dictionary` (ADR-0007), which the review checks and a heuristic rule flags (`for ... in <dictionary-typed name>`, advisory).
211	
212	**5.4 Integer discipline.** `INTEGER_DIVISION=2` makes every `/` on two integers a load error unless annotated. The repository has **exactly one** annotation: `@warning_ignore("integer_division")` on the `return a / b` statement in `IntMath.trunc_div` (`src/shared/int_math.gd`), checked by `SIM-05` (count of `integer_division` ignores under `src/` equals 1, located in that function). `IntMath` exposes `trunc_div`, `floor_div` (`trunc_div(a - posmod(a, b), b)`) and `posmod_i`; the P11 fixtures (`-181/256 = 0`, `-362/256 = -1`, `-768/256 = -3`, `floor_div(-1, 48) = -1`) are committed as the first unit test `tests/unit/shared/int_math_test.gd`. The `%` operator is not covered by an engine warning (a negative operand gives a negative remainder, P11), so `SIM-04` bans `%` on integers in `src/shared`, `src/kernel`, `src/sim` outside `IntMath` (a `%` following a string literal is formatting and is ignored; formatting is itself banned in hot code, § 7) and bans `min`, `max`, `clamp`, `abs`, `sign`, `floor`, `ceil`, `round`, `sqrt`, `pow`, `lerp` and `int(`/`float(` conversions in the same directories (use `mini`, `maxi`, `clampi`, `absi`, `signi`). This is the grep lint of TR-emitter-034 and TR-shipbody-002, generalised from "the Emitter directory" and "the Body and Layout directories" to the whole simulation, with committed bad/good fixtures per banned token.
213	
214	**5.5 Float-free simulation.** `SIM-03` bans `float` as a declaration or return type, float literals (a decimal point or exponent in a numeric token), `Vector2(`/`Vector3(`/`Transform2D` (use `Vector2i`), `INF`, `NAN`, `PI`, `TAU` in `src/shared`, `src/sim` and (outside the allow-list `float_allowlist.json`: `kernel_host.gd`, `presentation_clock.gd`, the diagnostics timer, the `*_read.gd` content readers) `src/kernel` and `src/data`. A lexical ban cannot see a float produced by an engine call that returns one; the engine tier (`NARROWING_CONVERSION`, `UNSAFE_*`, `INFERENCE_ON_VARIANT` at 2) catches the assignment, and the definitive check is runtime: ADR-0005's canonical encoder rejects a float in any snapshot (assumption recorded), so a float that reaches a block fails the first golden replay.
215	
216	### 6. The lint tool
217	
218	**6.1 Shape.** One headless GDScript runner, `tools/lint/lint_main.gd`, run as `godot --headless --path . -s res://tools/lint/lint_main.gd -- [--pack <name>] [--changed-since <rev>]`. Why GDScript and not `gdtoolkit` (Python): reflection and the class map exist only in-engine (P5); ADR-0007's `content_lint.gd` already makes GDScript the CI tool language and shares the `ContentLoader`; one binary on the CI runner; `gdtoolkit` 4.5.0 does not document the 4.5+ grammar (UNVERIFIED, checked 2026-10-28). `gdformat`/`gdlint` may be run **advisorily** by a developer; no blocking rule depends on them.
219	
220	- `tools/lint/core/`: `LintScanner` (the lexical front end), `LintRule`, `LintReport`, `LintConfig`.
221	- `tools/lint/<pack>_lint.gd`: one file per rule pack (`arch`, `sim`, `kernel`, `prj`, `alloc`, `msa`, ...). Owner ADRs add packs; TR-assembly-044's `tools/lint/msa_lint.gd` is such a pack.
222	- `tools/lint/config/*.json`: modules, edges, token lists, allow-lists (each entry `{path_glob, symbol, reason, owner, added}`), warning levels, kernel members, frozen classes, `owners.json`. These are tool configuration, parsed with `JSON.new()`; they are not game content.
223	
224	**6.2 Finding format and exit codes.** One line per finding: `LINT-<PACK>-<NN> <error|warn> <path>:<line>: <rule_name>: <message>` (for example `LINT-MSA-3 error src/sim/assembly/x.gd:42: ...`). Exit codes: **0** no findings at error severity; **1** at least one error finding; **2** tool failure (import cache missing, config unreadable, a rule threw). A `warn` finding never fails the run but is counted in the summary. Output is ordered by `(path, line, rule)` so two runs are byte-identical. The tool prints a summary of waivers in force.
225	
226	**6.3 The lexical front end and its limits (tier E2).** `LintScanner` strips `#` comments and string literals (including `"""` multi-line, `r"..."`, `&"..."`, `^"..."`, `$"..."`) while preserving line numbers, replaces each string with `""`, tracks `func` boundaries by indentation (so a rule can be scoped to a function name), and reads `## @hot` and `# lint-allow:` markers from the original text. It does **not** build an AST. Consequently it **can** see: tokens, counts, class names, call-site names, function names, decorators, `.tscn`/`project.godot`/`export_presets.cfg` text through `ConfigFile`; it **cannot** see: the static type of an expression, which object a method is called on, data flow, whether a write happens "inside a WriteScope", runtime process priorities. 322	### 9. GDExtension escape hatch (OQ-10)
323	
324	**9.1 Default.** The game ships **GDScript only** through MVP. Every performance budget is measured on a release export (R12) and "pending spike" until S1 reports. The ladder before native code is: **rung 0** as written; **rung 1** tuning inside the GDScript design (caps, divisors, data layout: structure-of-arrays, preallocated buffers, early-outs); **rung 2** call-overhead removal (caching accessors in locals, folding a `Callable.call` or a port dispatch out of an inner loop, merging passes; S1 measures "accessor and `Callable.call` overhead per ms"); **rung 3** a GDExtension. Rung 3 is allowed only for the Life-Support Graph's propagate phases (architecture: "Graph (rung 3, VS-A only)"), unless an ADR amendment names another pure function.
325	
326	**9.2 Trigger.** Rung 3 is entered only when S1 / SP-ENG-1 on RM-DECK (the slower reference) shows the stub-Graph P99 over its budget share **after** rung 1 and rung 2 are applied and recorded, and the technical-director accepts an amendment to this ADR (the `godot-gdextension-specialist` listed in `project.yaml` reviews it). It is never decided inside a story.
327	
328	**9.3 Constraints on any native module.**
329	- **Same seam, same behaviour.** The native module implements an `@abstract` port (for example `GraphPropagator`). The GDScript implementation is kept, is always built, remains the **golden reference** and the fallback, and the full test suite plus the replay `state_hash` comparison (ADR-0005) run against **both** implementations in CI; a divergence fails the build.
330	- **Integer-only, tree-free API.** Inputs and outputs are scalars and `PackedInt32Array`/`PackedInt64Array`; no `Node`, no engine singletons beyond array allocation, no threads, no floats, no RNG, no clock, no file I/O. C++ is compiled with `-fwrapv` (signed overflow wraps like GDScript's int64) and fixed-width integer types; no `-ffast-math`.
331	- **Platforms.** Windows x86_64 and Linux x86_64 (Steam Deck), built in CI as artifacts, not committed. Sources under `native/src/`, binaries under `native/bin/`, `native/<module>.gdextension` with `compatibility_minimum` set to 4.7. The matching `godot-cpp` branch for 4.7 is UNVERIFIED. Build system: SCons (the project's stated build system).
332	- **Selection** is made by the composition root (it constructs one implementation and injects it), not by a global flag read inside the simulation. A missing library in a development build falls back to GDScript and logs; a release export check asserts the library is packaged.
333	- **Not allowed:** C# (the mono editor is not the shipping runtime; CI and export templates are standard builds), GDExtension for presentation or `Node`-bound code, and any native code before the S1 evidence.

390	### Implementation Guidelines
391	
392	- **Must** place every script in the directory § 1.1 assigns and name it per § 1.2; **must never** create a top-level directory under `src/` or a module directory not listed in `modules.json`, and **must never** put sim code at `src/sanity/` or any path outside `src/sim/<system>/`.
393	- **Must** reach another module through its `class_name`; **must never** `preload`, `load` or `ResourceLoader` a `.gd` path in `src/`, and **must never** let `src/data/`, `src/save/` or `src/kernel/` name a `src/sim/` class.
394	- **Must** let presentation name only `sim/<x>/views/**`, `sim/<x>/ports/**` and `kernel/facets/**`; **must never** give a presentation, debug or observer file `Kernel`, `SimViews`, `WriteScope`, `Command` or a context class.
395	- **Must** express an injected seam as an `@abstract` port in the provider's `ports/` directory, restate the full signature in implementations and doubles, and take the port type in `setup()`; **must never** write `IFoo` names, an abstract `BlockOwner`, or a double that merely has matching method names without extending the port (use `ContractCheck` for the one case where it cannot).
396	- **Must** keep `src/shared`, `src/kernel`, `src/data`, `src/save`, `src/sim/**` free of the SIM-01 token list; **must never** attach a script from those directories to a scene, add an autoload, or declare a `static var`.
397	- **Must** put the PROJECTOR scripts in `src/presentation/projector/` and `KernelHost` in `src/game/`.
398	- **Must** use `IntMath.trunc_div`, `floor_div` and `posmod_i` for integer division and modulo in `shared`, `kernel`, `sim`; **must never** write `/` on two integers, `%` on integers, `min`/`max`/`clamp`/`abs`/`sign`/`floor`/`ceil`/`round`, a float, or add a second `@warning_ignore("integer_division")` there.
399	- **Must** keep all `debug/gdscript/warnings/*` at 2 (RETURN_VALUE_DISCARDED at 0) and the `directory_rules` of § 5.1; **must never** leave a warning at 1 or add a path to `directory_rules` with value 0 under `src/`.
400	- **Must** add the lint rule (and its bad/good fixtures) for a new constraint in the same story that introduces the code it constrains; **must never** state a rule as "lint-enforced" in a story without naming its rule id and tier.
401	- **Must** tag allocation-sensitive functions `## @hot`, keep them free of the HOT-01 tokens, and add the `CNT-01` to `CNT-03` assertions to the suite that exercises them; **must never** claim "zero allocation" without those checks.
402	- **Must** keep test seams in `src/<module>/testing/` classes named `Test*` and inject `WorkCounter`, `Clock` and similar through ports; **must never** read `OS.has_feature` or a compile flag to switch sim behaviour.
403	- **Must** put doubles and fakes in `tests/support/` and render-only suites in `tests/render/`; **must never** let a render-tagged check run in lane H or pass with a zero draw count.
404	- **Must** commit `addons/gdUnit4/` at the pinned version and treat exit 101 as failure; **must never** change the pin without repeating LINT-SPIKE-1(g).
405	- **Must** record any new waiver or allow-list entry with a reason and an owner; **must never** waive an NW rule.
406	- **Must** keep the GDScript implementation of any natively accelerated module as the golden reference; **must never** enter GDExtension rung 3 without the S1 evidence and an accepted amendment, and **must never** use C#.

408	## Alternatives Considered
409	
410	### Alternative 1: `gdtoolkit` (`gdlint`/`gdformat`, Python) as the lint tool
411	- **Description**: Run `gdlint` with custom Python checks over its parse tree in CI.

408	## Alternatives Considered
409	
410	### Alternative 1: `gdtoolkit` (`gdlint`/`gdformat`, Python) as the lint tool
411	- **Description**: Run `gdlint` with custom Python checks over its parse tree in CI.
412	- **Pros**: A real parse tree (lark grammar) for structural rules; mature formatter; no code to write for style rules.
413	- **Cons**: Latest release 4.5.0 (Oct 2025) documents no `@abstract`, variadic or 4.6/4.7 support (UNVERIFIED either way); a second toolchain (Python, pinned versions) beside the Godot binary; no reflection, no class map, no `ProjectSettings` access, so E3 rules would need a second tool anyway; cannot share `ContentLoader` with ADR-0007's lint.
414	- **Rejection Reason**: Correctness of blocking rules cannot depend on a parser whose 4.7 grammar coverage is unknown. It stays available for advisory formatting; a later ADR may adopt it for E2 rules after a grammar probe.
415	
416	### Alternative 2: Engine warnings and tests only, no lexical tool
417	- **Description**: Rely on warnings-as-errors, `@abstract`, and gdUnit4 tests for every rule.
418	- **Pros**: Zero tool code.
419	- **Cons**: The engine does not see tokens (`Time.get_ticks_usec`, `_physics_process`, `preload` of a sibling), import edges, `.tscn` priorities, or `%` on integers; tests only find a violation on a code path they execute.
420	- **Rejection Reason**: Roughly half of the inherited rules are lexical by nature (§ 6.6). The lexical tier is small and fixture-tested.
421	
422	### Alternative 3: A hand-written GDScript parser (real AST)
423	- **Description**: Write a GDScript parser in GDScript to decide type-aware rules (who writes a field, what is a float).
424	- **Pros**: Could express field-writer and scope rules exactly.
425	- **Cons**: A large, maintained component tracking a language that changed in 4.5, 4.6 and 4.7; type-flow rules duplicate the engine's analyzer, which is already authoritative and free.
426	- **Rejection Reason**: The engine analyzer (E1) covers type flow; reflection (E3) covers shape; runtime (E4) covers dynamic facts. What remains is honestly weaker (file/function granularity) and is documented as such.
427	
428	### Alternative 4: Duck-typed contracts checked by a boot-time registry lint
429	- **Description**: No base classes; each seam is a method-name list; a boot-time registry compares every injected object with the list via `has_method`.
430	- **Pros**: No dependence on `@abstract`; doubles are just objects.
431	- **Cons**: A missing method is found at boot or first call, not at parse time; checks only method names unless extended with reflection; `has_method` strings drift silently; no editor completion.
432	- **Rejection Reason**: `@abstract` gives a parse-time error on 4.7.2 (P4) for the same cost. The duck-typed form survives only as `ContractCheck` for recorded stubs.
433	
434	### Alternative 5: Two strictness tiers (sim strict, presentation lax) by warning severity
435	- **Description**: BDY-3's original idea: error severity for the Body and Layout directories only; filter CI output by path.
436	- **Pros**: Presentation authors face fewer errors.
437	- **Cons**: Severity is global per warning and directories only opt in or out (P2); a per-path tier needs severity 1, which is invisible headless (P10), so CI would need a second parse pipeline; presentation code that mixes ints and floats is exactly where an accidental `/` creeps into a sim-visible value (draw positions feed `world_to_hud`, aim, mouse).
438	- **Rejection Reason**: One tier for `src/` and `tools/` is simpler and fully engine-enforced; the extra annotation burden in presentation is small (typed locals, `IntMath`).
439	
440	### Alternative 6: Plain base class whose methods `push_error`
441	- **Description**: The architecture's stated fallback.
442	- **Pros**: Works even if `@abstract` misbehaves in export.
443	- **Cons**: A missing override is a runtime error on first call; no parse-time guarantee.
444	- **Rejection Reason**: Kept as the documented fallback (§ 3.4) behind the same call sites, used only if LINT-SPIKE-1(a) fails.
445	
446	### Alternative 7: Flat vertical-slice layout (`src/<feature>/{sim,presentation}`)
447	- **Description**: One directory per feature holding both its simulation and presentation code.
448	- **Pros**: Everything for a feature in one place.
449	- **Cons**: The most important import rule (simulation never reads presentation) stops being a directory test; per-directory tree-freedom, float-freedom and warning scope all become per-file; the architecture's layer table and the GDDs' paths already use `src/sim/<system>/`.
450	- **Rejection Reason**: A layer-first tree makes the architecture's central rules mechanical.
451	
452	### Alternative 8: C# or GDExtension-first for performance
453	- **Description**: Write the Graph and other hot code natively from the start.
454	- **Pros**: Predictable speed.
455	- **Cons**: No measurement justifies it (S1 pending); C# is outside the project's language and the shipping builds; native code before the design is stable multiplies change cost; determinism parity must be proven against a reference.
456	- **Rejection Reason**: Evidence-gated ladder (§ 9): GDScript first, native only on S1 evidence, GDScript kept as the reference.
457	
458	## Consequences
459	
460	### Positive
461	- "Simulation never reads presentation", "no `preload` of a sibling", "no wall-clock in the sim" and "no autoload" become build failures instead of review comments.
462	- The engine enforces typing and integer discipline on every script the game runs, with no tool code; BDY-3's unverified directory scope is resolved.
463	- A missing method in a test double or an implementation is a parse error, not a runtime surprise.
464	- Every "lint-enforced" requirement now names a rule id, a tier and its blind spots; OQ-16 is closed for its wording.
465	- Allocation claims have checks that exist, and the document says what each cannot see.
466	- One CI order puts parse and layering errors before test noise, and render checks cannot silently pass in a headless job.
467	- Native code has a written gate and a parity requirement, so it cannot arrive as a convenience.
468	
469	### Negative
470	- Everything under `src/` and `tools/` must be fully typed: no `:=`, no untyped locals, no `Variant` shortcuts. Authoring is slower, and engine-patch warning additions can break the build until classified (`PRJ-01`).
471	- The lexical tier is heuristic: it works at file and function granularity, cannot see types, and a stripped-string or continuation edge case is a tool bug to fix. Field-writer rules are weaker than a real AST would make them.
472	- Level-1 warnings are unusable headless, so the project loses the "warn but pass" middle state.
473	- `tests/` is excluded from the warning scope; test code is untyped-tolerant by design.
474	- Layering costs a `views/`/`ports/`/`facets/` convention that every module author must follow, and a module that needs a second-sim-module internal must go through its published surface.
475	- The windowed lane depends on hardware (a GPU runner, a Deck) the project may not have wired up.
476	
477	## Risks
478	- **`@abstract` does not survive a release export, or reflective construction creeps in.** Mitigation: LINT-SPIKE-1(a); fallback § 3.4 behind unchanged call sites; no game code constructs via `GDScript.new()`.
479	- **Warnings-as-errors makes a patch release unbuildable** (a new default-1 warning). Mitigation: `PRJ-01` names the unclassified warning; CI pins the exact engine version.
480	- **`directory_rules` behaves differently in an export or a later patch.** Mitigation: it is a project setting probed on 4.7.2; export compiles with the same analyzer; LINT-SPIKE-1 re-checks on the export; `load_all` runs on the exact CI binary.
481	- **Lexical false negatives** (a banned token built dynamically, `call("get_tree")`). Mitigation: dynamic dispatch by string is itself flagged in `shared`, `kernel`, `sim` (`SIM-12`); the runtime tier catches what reaches state.
482	- **Lexical false positives stall work.** Mitigation: per-line waivers with reasons, NW only for the few non-negotiable rules, fixtures for edge cases, a waiver baseline.
483	- **A rule is added by an owner ADR without fixtures or a tier.** Mitigation: `FIX-01` fails the suite; the inventory table is the checklist.
484	- **`MEMORY_STATIC` noise or release unavailability makes `CNT-02` flaky.** Mitigation: tolerance tuned by LINT-SPIKE-1; debug-binary-only; never a release gate; the other three tiers do not depend on it.
485	- **No windowed runner exists.** Mitigation: the lane report states "not run"; render ACs stay open rather than passing; the open question names the decision owner.
486	- **gdUnit4 6.2.2 is observed on 4.7.2 but not declared.** Mitigation: committed add-on, spike re-observation, upgrade only by amendment.
487	- **Presentation `views/` convention is violated because a read view's class lives inside a sim module's internals.** Mitigation: `ARCH-02` fails it; ADR-0009 and each module ADR place view classes in `views/`.

542	## Performance Implications
543	- **CPU (runtime):** None added to release builds: lint rules, `## @hot` tags and `directory_rules` have no run-time cost; boot walks and counters run in dev and test builds only. Full static typing lets the GDScript compiler use typed opcodes (`deprecated-apis.md`: typed variables have "GDScript compiler optimizations"; magnitude UNVERIFIED, S1 measures). rep(L,'- **Same seam, same behaviour.**','- **Same seam, same behaviour.** The port stays a GDScript `@abstract` class (for example `GraphPropagator`). A GDExtension class can extend only a native (ClassDB) class, never a GDScript class, so a native object is not `is GraphPropagator` and a `setup(p: GraphPropagator)` parameter would reject it. The extension therefore registers a plain `RefCounted`-derived native class (for example `GraphPropagatorNative`) with the same method set, and a thin GDScript adapter `NativeGraphPropagator extends GraphPropagator` owns the native object and forwards each call; the composition root injects the adapter, so call sites do not change. A `ContractCheck` fixture compares the native class\'s `ClassDB.class_get_method_list` with the port\'s `get_script_method_list()`. The GDScript implementation is kept, is always built, remains the **golden reference** and the fallback, and the full test suite plus the replay `state_hash` comparison (ADR-0005) run against **both** implementations in CI; a divergence fails the build.')

# Architecture Decision Registry

# PURPOSE: Single source of truth for key architectural stances that all ADRs
# must agree on. Skills check this before writing new ADRs to detect conflicts
# at authoring time — before stories are created against contradictory decisions.
#
# RULES:
#   - Register a stance when it constrains how OTHER systems must be built.

#     to be registered.

#     quoted: unquoted, the second colon makes the file invalid YAML.
#   - When a stance changes: update the entry, set revised: to today's date,
#     add a comment with the old value, and run /architecture-review to check

decisions.point: Rule id for the warning-waiver allow-list (E3)
decisions.chosen: PRJ-04 (NW, E2), with SIM-05 as its special case
decisions.reason: Scope covers tools/ as well as src/, so a SIM-prefixed id would mislead; the engine raises the warnings so lint-allow cannot waive them.

decisions.point: Where the WallClock port lives (T4 versus TD-11)
decisions.chosen: src/save/wall_clock.gd, implemented by src/game/system_wall_clock.gd, which is the fourth SIM-02 allow-list entry
decisions.reason: TD-11 keeps wall time out of the kernel and injects it only into SaveService.setup(); OQ-D closed.

decisions.point: IntMath divisor guard versus SIM-11 (no assert in src/)
decisions.chosen: Follow TD-12 (b <= 0 returns 0 with a debug assert); admit that assert as the single SIM-11 allow-list entry and give its log line a suite-scoped lane-H allow-list entry
decisions.reason: The assert sits beside a defined release result and carries no invariant; whether a failed assert aborts the helper in a headless debug run is UNVERIFIED (LINT-SPIKE-1(j)).

decisions.point: SIM-04 scope for / and % (E2 versus TD-14)
decisions.chosen: Operator tokens /, %, /=, %= banned outright in shared, kernel and sim outside src/shared/int_math.gd; det_rng_float.gd exempt only for float( and floor
decisions.reason: A lexical scan cannot know operand types; Vector2i division escapes INTEGER_DIVISION. Vector helpers and a possible / in det_rng_float.gd are requested of ADR-0005 (OQ-N).

decisions.chosen: Explicit tick-phase list (Kernel, SimViews, WriteScope, Command, BlockDescriptor, CallContext, ValidateContext, ApplyContext, HookContext, SnapshotContext); no *Context glob; NotifyFacet named only by src/game and PresentationFacet
decisions.reason: Presenter handlers legitimately take NotifyContext and return CompletionToken; TD-01 prevails over the T1 amendment.

decisions.chosen: src/presentation/pipeline/; no src/presentation/common/
decisions.reason: PipelineRoot is the PresentationHost; ARCH-01 and modules.json need no change.

decisions.chosen: src/game/save_host.gd, Node, ProcessPriority.HOST_SERVICE (-40), named only there and in process_priority.gd (KRN-03, KRN-05)

registry_candidates.name: source_layout
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- purpose: source_layout
    status: active           # ADR-0010 is Proposed
    api: "Layer-first tree: src/shared (L0, imports nothing; scene-tree-free, I/O-free, no global state; IntMath and src/shared/det), src/kernel and src/data and src/save (L1; save is RefCounted only), src/sim/<system> for graph, layout, body, emitter, controller, interaction, suit, assembly, web, attention, horror, sanity (L2), src/presentation/<system> for pipeline, perception, lighting, trail, hud, instruments, chart, audio, controller, projector (L3; shared presentation files in pipeline/), src/game (composition root, KernelHost src/game/kernel_host.gd, SaveHost src/game/save_host.gd, MonotonicClock, SystemWallClock), src/debug and src/observer (dev only, guarded load); published surfaces are kernel/facets (the presentation-visible kernel API list), kernel/ports, sim/<x>/views, sim/<x>/ports; test seams only in src/<module>/testing/"

    reason: "Makes simulation-never-reads-presentation, tree-freedom and warning scope directory tests, and resolves IC-10"

    revised: ""

registry_candidates.name: integer_division_outside_int_math
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:

    status: active           # ADR-0010 is Proposed
    description: "The operator tokens /, %, /= and %= appear only inside IntMath in shared, kernel and sim; there is exactly one @warning_ignore(\"integer_division\") in src/, on IntMath.trunc_div; min, max, clamp, abs, sign, floor, ceil, round and trig functions are not used on simulation values (use mini, maxi, clampi, absi, signi)."
    why: "Negative operands truncate toward zero and % keeps the sign (probed on 4.7.2); Vector2i division truncates silently and escapes INTEGER_DIVISION; one tested site removes the class of off-by-one bugs."

decisions.point: IntMath divisor guard versus SIM-11 (no assert in src/)
decisions.chosen: Follow TD-12 (b <= 0 returns 0 with a debug assert); admit that assert as the single SIM-11 allow-list entry and give its log line a suite-scoped lane-H allow-list entry

decisions.reason: A lexical scan cannot know operand types; Vector2i division escapes INTEGER_DIVISION. Vector helpers and a possible / in det_rng_float.gd are requested of ADR-0005 (OQ-N).

decisions.point: SIM-04 scope for / and % (E2 versus TD-14)
decisions.chosen: Operator tokens /, %, /=, %= banned outright in shared, kernel and sim outside src/shared/int_math.gd; det_rng_float.gd exempt only for float( and floor
decisions.reason: A lexical scan cannot know operand types; Vector2i division escapes INTEGER_DIVISION. Vector helpers and a possible / in det_rng_float.gd are requested of ADR-0005 (OQ-N).

decisions.chosen: Explicit tick-phase list (Kernel, SimViews, WriteScope, Command, BlockDescriptor, CallContext, ValidateContext, ApplyContext, HookContext, SnapshotContext); no *Context glob; NotifyFacet named only by src/game and PresentationFacet
decisions.reason: Presenter handlers legitimately take NotifyContext and return CompletionToken; TD-01 prevails over the T1 amendment.

decisions.reason: PipelineRoot is the PresentationHost; ARCH-01 and modules.json need no change.
